title: Editor game speed quantizes effective physics tick rate to integer values
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible on current `master`, also in steam version.

### System information

Windows 11 - Godot 4.7.1.stable - Nvidia RTX 4050 Laptop GPU

### Issue description

The effective physics tick rate used by the editor Game Speed control is currently stored as an integer.

This causes fractional effective tick rates to be truncated. For example, with the default 60 physics ticks per second and a Game Speed of 1/16x:


60 * 1/16 = 3.75


However, the effective physics tick rate becomes 3 instead of 3.75.

As a result, physics is not scheduled at exactly the speed selected in the Game Speed control.

This is related to #122217, where the same integer quantization also resulted in an incorrect physics delta. The delta issue can be fixed separately, but the effective physics scheduling rate is still quantized.

For example, fractional rates below 1 Hz should also be representable. With 8 physics ticks per second at 1/16x speed, the effective rate should be:


8 * 1/16 = 0.5 Hz

### Steps to reproduce

Attach this script to a Node.

extends Node

var physics_calls := 0
var start_time := 0
var last_report_time := 0

func _ready() -> void:
	start_time = Time.get_ticks_msec()
	last_report_time = start_time

	print("Physics ticks per second: ", Engine.physics_ticks_per_second)
	print("Set editor Game Speed to 1/16x")
	print("Expected effective rate at 60 TPS: 3.75 physics calls/sec")
	print("Expected physics delta: ", 1.0 / Engine.physics_ticks_per_second)

func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	physics_calls += 1

	var now := Time.get_ticks_msec()

	if now - last_report_time >= 4000:
		var elapsed_sec := float(now - last_report_time) / 1000.0
		var measured_rate := physics_calls / elapsed_sec

		print("")
		print("---- RESULT ----")
		print("Physics calls: ", physics_calls)
		print("Measured real-world rate: ", measured_rate, " calls/sec")
		print("Current delta: ", delta)
		print("Expected delta: ", 1.0 / Engine.physics_ticks_per_second)

		if is_equal_approx(delta, 1.0 / Engine.physics_ticks_per_second):
			print("DELTA: PASS")
		else:
			print("DELTA: FAIL")

		if measured_rate > 3.4 and measured_rate < 4.1:
			print("FRACTIONAL RATE: PASS (~3.75 Hz)")
		elif measured_rate > 2.7 and measured_rate < 3.3:
			print("FRACTIONAL RATE: FAIL (looks rounded to ~3 Hz)")
		else:
			print("FRACTIONAL RATE: unexpected value")

		print("----------------")

		physics_calls = 0
		last_report_time = now
